meta_title: Install VpnHood! SERVER on Linux | VpnHood!
meta_description: Install VpnHood! SERVER on Linux from VpnHood! MANAGER, or as a standalone server with one command, then create the access keys your devices connect with.
title: Install VpnHood! SERVER
lead: Run your own VPN server on any Linux machine with a public IP address. VpnHood! MANAGER can install it for you as a managed server, or one command installs it as a standalone server.
flow_server_desc: VpnHood! SERVER runs on a machine you control, such as a VPS.
flow_key_desc: MANAGER or the server creates it. Whoever has the key can connect.
flow_devices_desc: Add the key to VpnHood! CLIENT on a phone or a computer.
req_machine: A machine with a public IP address, running Linux on x64 or arm64.
req_admin: Root access. The install commands run through sudo, so it has to be on the machine even if you sign in as root.
req_port: TCP port [server_port] open, both in the machine's firewall and in your hosting provider's. It is the port the server listens on.
req_udp: The server's UDP port open the same way, for the devices that use UDP: a closed port leaves them without traffic. A standalone server picks this port at its first start and keeps it in [server_udp_port_file], and its log names it. On a managed server, it is the [manager_udp_port] of its address in MANAGER.
mgr_add: VpnHood! MANAGER installs the server for you and issues its access keys. In MANAGER, open [manager_servers], select [manager_add], name the server and select [manager_create]. MANAGER then shows the ways to install it:
shot_alt: The ways VpnHood! MANAGER offers to install a new server
mgr_ssh: [manager_install_ssh_password] or [manager_install_ssh_key]: give MANAGER the machine's address and an account with root access, and it signs in over SSH and installs the server itself. MANAGER has to reach the machine's SSH port, [port_ssh] unless you changed it. For a key, upload its file with [manager_upload_ssh_key].
mgr_command: [manager_install_command]: run the command MANAGER shows on the machine. It is the standalone installer below, with the settings that connect the server to MANAGER, and it asks the same two questions. Keep the command private: it holds the server's credentials.
mgr_appsettings: [manager_install_manual]: for a server you installed already. Save the settings MANAGER shows as [server_appsettings], then restart the server with [server_restart_linux].
mgr_status: The server connects to MANAGER over HTTPS, at [manager_agent_host]. Once it does, its status changes from [manager_not_installed] to [manager_idle], and to [manager_active] while devices are connected. To see the install options again, open the server and select [manager_install], or [manager_reinstall] once it is installed.
mgr_keys: Then create the access keys for your devices in MANAGER, under [manager_access_tokens].
step_linux_run: Run this command. It detects whether the machine is x64 or arm64, installs the server into [server_dir_linux] and asks you two questions.
step_linux_autostart: When it asks [autostart_prompt_linux] and [autoupdate_prompt_linux], press Enter for both. The server then runs as a service: it starts with the machine, starts again after a crash, and keeps itself up to date.
caption_unattended: In a script, install without the questions
step_key_run: A standalone server lets in only devices that hold an access key it made. Run this on the server to create one.
step_key_copy: The key is printed under [accesskey_heading] and starts with [key_prefix]; copy the whole line. A few lines above it, [hostendpoints_label] should show your server's public IP address.
key_options: To limit a key, add any of these options to the command.
opt_name: A name, to tell your keys apart.
opt_max_client: How many devices can use the key at the same time. Without it: 2.
opt_max_traffic: A traffic limit, in megabytes. Without it: none.
opt_max_speed: A speed limit for both upload and download, in megabits per second. Without it: none.
opt_expire: The day the key stops working. Without it: never.
caption_example: For example, a key for one phone that stops working at the end of 2030
note_key_secret: Anyone who has the key can connect through your server. Share it the way you would share a password.
step_connect: Install VpnHood! CLIENT on each device, add the key, and connect.
manage_linux: The server runs as the [server_service] service, whether it is managed or standalone.
manage_manual: If you installed it without the service, start it yourself with [vhserver_run]. It runs until you stop it with [vhserver_stop] from another terminal.
updates_desc: Unless you turned it off at install, the server updates itself to each new release: the [server_updater] service checks every 12 hours.
updates_off: To turn this off, run the standalone install command again and answer [answer_no] to [autoupdate_prompt_linux]. The installer keeps your answer and your settings, so the server stays on its version until you run the command yourself. In a script, add [flag_no_auto_update]:
updates_keep: Keep updates on if you can. Some releases fix security issues, and newer apps may stop supporting old servers.
